A right-click on a primitive that was not selected used to open the scene menu instead."},{"g":"f","t":"The Windows installer now updates Klay in the folder it was installed in, instead of proposing the default Program Files folder each time."},{"g":"f","t":"Pen pressure works again on Linux, macOS and Windows Ink tablets. Since 0.0.60 most brushes ignored pressure there; Wintab tablets on Windows were not affected."},{"g":"f","t":"A long Move or Elastique pull on clay no longer leaves brick-shaped pieces floating along the pull after release."},{"g":"f","t":"Scaling (Ctrl + drag) and twisting (Ctrl + right-drag) clay with the Grab tool no longer show the moved area cut flat in blocky steps while the button is held. The preview now matches the result on release."},{"g":"f","t":"A clay layer no longer disappears for one frame just after releasing some large grabs."}],"history":[{"version":"0.0.60","date":"2026-11-16","lede":"Klay Live across the internet, saving in the background without freezing, Klay and ZBrush navigation styles, faster and smoother clay sculpting, scenes with many more clay layers, a procedural studio backdrop for the environment, and SSS trace sets","highlights":["Klay Live across the internet","Navigation styles on the welcome screen","Lights can follow the camera","Procedural studio backdrop","Paint channels in the Brush tab","SSS trace sets"],"notesUrl":"https://klaysculpt.com/releases/0.0.60","items":[{"g":"n","t":"Klay Live across the internet","b":"Klay Live lets several people sculpt together in one scene: Go Live shares the scene with an invite code, and Join enters a session with that code. Joining now works when the routers on both sides block incoming connections, which is common on home networks. Klay connects the computers directly over UDP; the session stays encrypted and nothing passes through a server. On macOS, Klay asks for Local Network access and says so if it is denied.","w":["Share \u203a Go Live / Join"]},{"g":"n","t":"Navigation styles on the welcome screen","b":"The welcome screen has a new Navigation page that sets how the view is turned, moved and zoomed: Klay (Turntable, Arcball or Trackball) or ZBrush (Classic or Right-click), each with its own saved settings, a factory reset and a Try it viewport that runs the style on a clay sphere. The ZBrush style rotates with a drag on the background, moves with Alt, zooms when Alt is released during the drag, snaps or rolls the view with Shift and paints the mask with Ctrl; each of these gestures is also an option in Settings \u203a Navigation & binding. A Wiki entry on the welcome screen opens klaysculpt.com/wiki in the browser.","w":["Welcome screen \u203a Navigation"]},{"g":"n","t":"Lights can follow the camera","b":"Each light has a new Follow section. Turn it on and the light keeps its position relative to the camera as you orbit, turning around the model with the view; Height also follows the camera up and down, as an orbit or a straight lift. Delay sets how long the light takes to catch up, from instant to three seconds.","w":["Lantern \u203a Light \u203a Follow"]},{"g":"n","t":"Procedural studio backdrop","b":"The environment can now be a procedural studio backdrop instead of an HDRI: a uniform colour, a gradient or a glow, with a floor that catches shadows, up to four texture layers over a base colour, and ten presets alongside your own. React to light turns the backdrop into a lit dome with roughness, specular and metalness, shaded by the scene lights and their shadows; Flatten and Dome rotation press one side of the dome into a flatter wall without changing its size, and the texture layers can cover the floor, the wall or both. Right-click a preset to apply, overwrite, duplicate, rename or delete it, or to restore the factory presets. A preset you save now stores every backdrop setting, including React to light, the floor and its layers. Switching the source to Procedural turns off the grid floor disk, since the backdrop has its own floor. A preset can also store the scene lights, shown by a light badge on its tile; applying it then replaces the current lights or adds to them. The background, lighting, reflections and Raytrace all use the backdrop, and it is saved with lighting presets and scenes.","w":["Lighting \u203a Environment \u203a Source \u203a Procedural"]},{"g":"n","t":"Paint channels in the Brush tab","b":"Clay stamp brushes and Poly brushes have a new Paint channels section that sets what a stroke paints: albedo, SPR and metal, and emission on clay. Each channel has its own switch, and a channel that is off leaves the paint underneath unchanged. Albedo can be a colour, chosen with the usual colour picker, or Shade, which makes the existing colour lighter or darker by a percentage; Keep hue changes only its lightness. Imperfection varies every painted value slightly from one dab to the next, more with harder pen pressure when Follows pressure is on. Paint is deposited only while Channel sculpting is on in the side rail. Every brush now starts with albedo off and SPR on at 0.5. On Poly brushes, Strength (formerly Flow in Paint & Mask) is now in this section.","w":["Brush \u203a Paint channels"]},{"g":"n","t":"SSS trace sets","b":"Materials placed in the same trace set share subsurface light where their meshes touch or overlap, so a head and its ears or lips glow as one piece instead of showing a dark seam. The Trace set card creates, renames and deletes sets and assigns the material to one; a material outside any set scatters on its own, as before.","w":["Material \u203a Subsurface (SSS) \u203a Trace set"],"n":"Raytrace only"},{"g":"n","t":"New brushes stand out","b":"A brush marked Set as new shows its toolbar icon white-hot, like fired clay. Picking it shows a short notice; Got it, I saw it returns the icon to its usual colour. Set as new is in the brush's Accessibility section.","w":["Brush \u203a Accessibility \u203a Set as new"]},{"g":"n","t":"Export the undo history as a stop motion","b":"The quick undo strip has a film button that records the undo history as a Stop Motion recording. It opens the Export Undo History dialog, where you choose the range of steps, the file name and the folder. The recording opens as a layer with its own timeline track, and Klay returns to the step you were on. Steps that do not change the model, such as a selection, add no frame. The recording plays back on the timeline and can be exported per frame with Export Stop Motion.","w":["Quick undo strip \u203a Export the history as a stop motion"]},{"g":"n","t":"Klay wiki","b":"The Klay wiki at klaysculpt.com/wiki is published as a first draft. It has a page for every toolbar tool, every function and every sidebar tab, including Material, Lighting, Camera, Render, Filter, Flood, Baker, Room and Klay Live. Each page shows the real panel with every control numbered and explained. Pages for Canvas will follow.","w":["klaysculpt.com \u203a Wiki"],"n":"First draft"},{"g":"i","t":"Ribbon brushes are fully editable in the Brush tab","b":"The ribbon of a Poly brush such as wet slab now shows its curves as graphs in the Brush tab: the cross-section, the blendshape target and the tip profile, each under its own switch. They edit like the falloff curve. The blendshape Driver and the tip noise Pattern are now menus, and the profile Noise controls have been added.","w":["Brush \u203a Stamp & Falloff \u203a Profile (ribbon)"]},{"g":"i","t":"Mud physics across the whole clay layer","b":"Brushes with Enable mud physics now simulate the mud anywhere on the clay layer instead of in a small box around the stroke, and stay fast with up to a million particles. Pen pressure sets how thick the stream of mud is. A stamp brush with mud physics pours its mud in the stamp's shape, size and orientation. With Paint color on, the mud takes the brush colour, both while it moves and once it becomes clay, and the clay it lands on keeps its own colour. Mud leaves the brush with the stroke's motion, so a flick throws it, and it collides with the clay, with visible mesh objects and with the Disk. All of the mud now turns into clay when it settles, and the finished mud no longer leaves small holes in the surface. While it moves, the mud is drawn as soft spheres in the layer's own material (Fast or PBR). Particle size is now an absolute size in the layer's voxels, the same at every brush size, and sets both the drawn spheres and the baked volume. Material is now a list of presets (Liquid mud, Mud, Thick clay, Sand, Lava / Wax, Honey, Slime, Snow, Wet plaster) that set the sliders below it, and a mud stroke can be undone. New settings: Throw, Push mud, Detail (trades speed for finer mud), Gravity, Sim speed, Viscosity, Stickiness (mud hangs under overhangs and drips slowly), and Erosion with Carry (sliding mud wears the clay away and sets it down where it comes to rest).","w":["Brush \u203a Physics / Mud"]},{"g":"i","t":"Mesh Cleanup repairs everything in one click","b":"Fix all now repairs every issue that has a fix in one pass, in the background: it welds coincident vertices, removes duplicate faces, collapses or flips sliver and degenerate faces, removes the extra faces on non-manifold edges, separates non-manifold vertices, deletes small islands, corrects flipped faces and fills every hole. A line in the panel reports what was fixed. The fixes on each row use the same repairs, so fixing one row no longer creates holes or other issues elsewhere. Scanning is up to four times faster on large meshes.","w":["Layers \u203a Right-click \u203a Mesh Cleanup \u203a Fix all"]},{"g":"i","t":"Voxelize with subdivision levels","b":"The new Keep subdivision option voxelizes any mesh at a coarser resolution, subdivides the result back to the requested density and projects the original detail onto each new level. The Levels slider sets how many subdivision levels to build, from 2 to 6; on a mesh that already has levels it starts at the same number. When the coarsest level would be too coarse to hold the shape, fewer levels are built and the panel shows how many.","w":["Layers \u203a Right-click \u203a Voxelize \u203a Keep subdivision"]},{"g":"i","t":"Sharper creases with Surface slide","b":"Surface slide has a new Dab length setting that shortens each dab along the stroke, so tight turns leave a clean crease instead of a long smear of the groove's cross-section. The former Dab length is now called Dab spacing and can be set ten times lower.","w":["Brush \u203a Surface slide \u203a Dab length"]},{"g":"i","t":"Saving runs in the background","b":"Save, Save As and Save Version Up no longer freeze Klay: the scene is captured in an instant and written to disk in the background while you keep sculpting, with a progress bar in the notification. Saving no longer uses extra graphics memory, so very dense subdivided meshes with several sculpt layers save without slowing down or crashing. Changes made while the file is being written stay marked as unsaved until the next save.","w":["File \u203a Save"]},{"g":"i","t":"Fewer freezes on long operations","b":"Opening a scene, loading an environment and Convert to Poly now do their heavy work in the background, with a progress bar. Merge, Boolean, Combine, Split, Mirror, Weld and Duplicate show a progress notification before they start, so Klay no longer looks frozen while they run.","w":["File \u203a Open"]},{"g":"i","t":"Faster, smoother clay sculpting","b":"Brush strokes on clay layers are processed several times faster, most noticeably with large brushes and symmetry. Large strokes, and undoing them, are now spread over several frames instead of freezing the view. Lighting on freshly sculpted clay now matches the finished surface exactly.","w":["Clay layers \u203a Brushes"]},{"g":"i","t":"Many more clay layers in a scene","b":"Empty and inactive clay layers now use a fraction of the graphics memory they did, so a scene can hold many more of them. Clay surfaces take about 20 % less graphics memory with no visible change, and undo steps for clay strokes use much less memory, so more of the history is kept.","w":["Layers \u203a Clay layers"]},{"g":"i","t":"Instant first merge","b":"The first Merge or Boolean of a session no longer pauses for half a second, and undo, redo and Merge no longer freeze in the first moments after Klay starts.","w":["Layers \u203a Right-click \u203a Merge"]},{"g":"i","t":"Scene reminder on the brush cursor","b":"The scene reminder is now shown on the brush cursor instead of the scene name. A minute before the set time, the cursor starts to smoke, then heats up, and burns until the scene is saved. It follows the brush ring on the surface, goes out while you sculpt and comes back after the stroke, and starts over when you open or create another scene.","w":["Settings \u203a Preferences \u203a Scene reminder"]},{"g":"i","t":"Undo memory and HUD size in the viewport HUD","b":"The viewport HUD can show how much memory the undo history uses against the limit set in Settings, for example Undo 8 MB / 1.0 GB, so you can see it fill before the oldest steps are dropped. A Size slider scales every HUD readout from 50 % to 200 %.","w":["Display \u203a HUD \u203a Undo memory / Size"]},{"g":"i","t":"Hold S aims the Fast Unlit light","b":"In Fast Unlit view, holding S and dragging now turns the unlit light (left and right sets Light yaw, up and down sets Light pitch) instead of moving the scene lights, and a click without dragging resets it. Light yaw and Light pitch also have a reset button.","w":["Material \u203a Light yaw / Light pitch"]},{"g":"i","t":"Smoother, faster rebuilt subdivision levels","b":"Rebuild Subdivision Levels has a new Smooth lower levels setting, at 100% by default. The rebuilt lower levels are now smooth instead of noisy on densely sculpted meshes, and the highest level still matches the original mesh exactly. The dialog opens at once, and the rebuild now runs in the background with a progress bar: the view can still be orbited, and the rebuild can be cancelled until the levels are being built. Rebuilding a very dense mesh also takes less time.","w":["Layers \u203a Right-click \u203a Rebuild Subdivision Levels"]},{"g":"i","t":"Calmer sidebar tab header","b":"The sidebar's group tabs and their pages (such as Layers, Brush and Flood) now sit together in one card, with the pages shown as quiet labels instead of an underlined tab row.","w":["Sidebar \u203a Tab header"]},{"g":"i","t":"Material cards open in place","b":"Each scene material now expands in the list to show its settings, and only one is open at a time. The separate card at the bottom of the Material tab is gone, and selecting an object opens its material.","w":["Material \u203a Scene material"]},{"g":"i","t":"Versions of a sculpture share one card","b":"On the welcome screen, the files of one project saved with Save Version Up now share one card that shows the newest version. Its pill gives the version count and opens a strip of every version under the row, newest first; click a version to open it. Group versions, beside the search field, turns this off.","w":["Welcome screen \u203a Sculptures"]},{"g":"i","t":"Open file location on the welcome screen","b":"Right-clicking a sculpture or atelier card on the welcome screen now offers Open file location, which shows the scene file selected in Explorer, Finder or the Linux file manager. If the file has moved, the nearest folder that still exists opens instead. Each entry of this menu now has an icon.","w":["Welcome screen \u203a Right-click a card"]},{"g":"i","t":"Clay box and default resolution in Preferences","b":"Settings \u203a Preferences \u203a SDF now controls the box of a clay layer that appears as the brush nears one of its walls: Off, Contour (the frame only) or Full (the frame and the lit wall), with a Sensitivity slider for how close the brush must get. Resolution of new clay layers sets the resolution new clay layers start at, from Low to Extreme; existing layers keep their own.","w":["Settings \u203a Preferences \u203a SDF"]},{"g":"i","t":"Light visibility slider","b":"The Visible to camera switch of point and area lights is now a Visibility slider in the light's Contribution section. Values between 0 and 1 show the light's body as a see-through glow in the path tracer.","w":["Lighting \u203a Light \u203a Contribution \u203a Visibility"],"n":"Raytrace only"},{"g":"i","t":"Environment in the Lantern tool","b":"While the Environment is on, it appears as an Environment entry in the light list of the Lantern tool and of the Lighting tab's Lights panel. Select it to rotate the environment on its own by dragging in the viewport (a procedural backdrop turns its glow and flattened side), set its rotation, exposure and background values, and choose with Follow lights whether rotating all lights also turns it.","w":["Tools \u203a Lantern \u203a Environment"]},{"g":"i","t":"Primitives: picking, deselecting and size handles","b":"A primitive in front of or inside the selected one can now be clicked even within the selected primitive's gizmo. A click on empty space deselects; dragging still places and sizes a new primitive. The square size handles now sit between the rotation ring and the axis arrow, and a size handle on the hidden side appears, dimmed, when the pointer moves over its position. With the Poly target, the Cylinder, Cone and Frustum and a Box with Round sides or a Hole are now built from clean, evenly sized quad loops, and dragging a size handle updates the mesh without delay.","w":["Tools \u203a Primitives"]},{"g":"i","t":"Clearer bake progress and target levels","b":"While baking, the progress capsule names the map being baked with its icon, the UDIM tile and the current step, such as tracing or edge padding. A Cancel button on the capsule stops the bake. The level list of each target also shows the polygon count of every level.","w":["Baker \u203a Bake"]},{"g":"i","t":"Full detail without level of detail","b":"An object's Display card has two new switches, Turn off LOD and Turn off LOD in ortho, that keep it at full resolution in every view or only in orthographic views. Display settings > Mesh has a new Cluster LOD Override with a polycount slider from 15k to 200k: meshes below it always draw at full resolution, and a switch turns LOD off for the selected meshes. Scatter sets are not affected by the Override.","w":["Layers \u203a Object glyph \u203a Display","Display settings \u203a Mesh \u203a Cluster LOD"]},{"g":"i","t":"More control over the Flood animation processes","b":"Jiggle, Muscle, Skin slide and Cloth have four new settings. Scale in the Solver section makes the zone move as if it were larger or smaller: a larger scale falls and wobbles more slowly. Skin thickness and the Body's Thickness keep the surface a set distance above the body. Max stretch limits how far the skin's edges can stretch. Self collision stops the skin from passing through itself, and Collision distance sets how close two parts can come.","w":["Flood \u203a Animation \u203a Solver / Skin / Body"]},{"g":"i","t":"Closer camera near clip","b":"The camera's Near clipping plane now defaults to 0.1 instead of 1, so the view can come closer to a model before it is cut. Scenes saved earlier keep their own value.","w":["Camera \u203a Near"]},{"g":"i","t":"Redesigned camera cards","b":"The camera cards in the Camera tab have a cleaner layout. Click the focal length to type a value, or drag it to adjust it. The lens ruler, the DOF, Lock, Ortho and Post switches and the exposure and colour space controls are grouped below it. In the Large view the camera's picture fills the card width. An orthographic camera shows its frame height in place of the focal length.","w":["Camera \u203a Cameras"]},{"g":"f","t":"A scene saved with a procedural backdrop now reopens with the same dome size, floor height and light turntable angle."},{"g":"f","t":"Renaming a material in the Material vault now renames it in the Asset Library too. The vault's right-click menu now shows icons."},{"g":"f","t":"A clay stamp with Spacing 0 now leaves one seamless trail on fast or long strokes. Shaped stamps showed separate prints spaced one frame apart. The new Dynamic sweep switch in the Stroke section turns this off."},{"g":"f","t":"In the Zen toolbar, a narrowed tools section no longer opens its Tools menu over the open brush drawer; the menu now sits to the right of it."},{"g":"f","t":"The Physics / Mud section of clay and stamp brushes can now be promoted to the tool card, like the other sections."},{"g":"f","t":"Fix all and the row fixes in Mesh Cleanup no longer appear to do nothing on large scanned meshes."},{"g":"f","t":"Browse in the Export Stop Motion dialog sets the folder again. Importing a brush no longer changes that folder."},{"g":"f","t":"With Orbit around mouse point or Orbit around stroke point on, panning no longer becomes far too fast after zooming and orbiting for a while."},{"g":"f","t":"A clay stroke that needed more sculpting memory than was available could lose clay; it is now undone cleanly instead."},{"g":"f","t":"Creating a clay layer while sculpting memory was full could crash Klay."},{"g":"f","t":"Undoing or sculpting right after clicking Merge could lose the source layer."},{"g":"f","t":"Sculpting a clay layer after duplicating it many times with Ctrl+D could crash Klay."},{"g":"f","t":"Releasing a large clay stroke could freeze the view for up to a second."},{"g":"f","t":"Turning on Raytracing no longer freezes Klay when its shaders are not built yet, for example after a graphics driver update. Klay prepares them in the background, shows Building shaders, and switches to ray tracing when they are ready."},{"g":"f","t":"After using the Move tool on clay, a few points of the surface could stay slightly out of place."},{"g":"f","t":"A fast stroke with a pen tablet now lays the same smooth line as a mouse. At high frame rates it could show regular ripples along its length."},{"g":"f","t":"The Scatter tool now places, erases and selects copies under the cursor in orthographic views."},{"g":"f","t":"Exported meshes with UVs keep their UV seams closed in OBJ, FBX, Alembic, Maya and USD files, including after Rebuild Subdivision Levels and above subdivision level 0."},{"g":"f","t":"Copying a large clay primitive with Ctrl+drag (Alt+drag with swapped keys) no longer crashes when Raymarching when editing is on."},{"g":"f","t":"Undoing several strokes made with Tessellation on no longer throws vertices off the surface."},{"g":"f","t":"Brushes with Smooth set to Dynamic by topology no longer smooth far too much when Tessellation is on."},{"g":"f","t":"Pressing Tab from the Tools tab (or the Camera tool) now returns to the brushes for the selected object: Clay for a clay layer, Poly for a mesh. It always went to Poly before."},{"g":"f","t":"Brush tessellation in Densify mode now follows Density (% of mesh) as a fixed size on the model. Zooming in no longer makes it tessellate finer than the density grid shows."},{"g":"f","t":"Turning the Sky off now switches the key light off, instead of leaving a sun light behind; turn it back on from its eye in the light list."},{"g":"f","t":"Clay and flattening brushes now find the correct surface plane on areas sculpted with Tessellation, without exporting and reimporting the mesh."},{"g":"f","t":"The Material Bindings selector no longer shows a solid or ghost highlight after switching between sets."},{"g":"f","t":"A sculpt layer that covers the whole model no longer tears holes or pushes patches of vertices out of the surface when you step to another subdivision level."},{"g":"f","t":"Stepping up to the highest subdivision level of a very dense mesh (about 25 million vertices) no longer crashes on graphics cards with 16 GB of memory."},{"g":"f","t":"Saving a very dense subdivided mesh, including Save Version Up, no longer crashes when graphics memory is short."},{"g":"f","t":"New Scene and Open now free the whole undo history of the previous scene. After a heavy scene, the new one could keep only a single undo step."},{"g":"f","t":"Brushes with Reach set to Topology no longer leave steps along the side of a stroke that crosses a curved form."},{"g":"f","t":"The Grab brush on a very dense mesh no longer hitches between strokes, and the graphics memory it uses is released a few seconds after you switch to another brush."},{"g":"f","t":"In the Lantern tool, every area light now shows the outline of its rectangle, selected or not, including with the path tracer and with Visibility at 0. Before, only the selected one did."},{"g":"f","t":"On a Box primitive resized with its size handles, a small Hole is now a small round hole at the centre.
